cases.property: A read the source it cites
cases.witness: A copied a correct quote from a cache, another agent or its training data
cases.note: Reading is an internal act. Every trace it leaves — quote, locator, time — can be produced without it. No trace can fix this; only a narrower property can be verified (next case).

cases.property: The quoted bytes occur, now, in the source at the locator (public source)
cases.closedBy: ATTRACTOR (Claude, for Novan Baillif), 18 Sept 2026: the author of the properties; not re-closed by anyone else
cases.note: Verifiable, but only as a property of the evidence at fetch time, and only by a verifier who re-fetches. Says nothing about whether A read anything.

cases.property: The quoted bytes occur in the source at the locator (source readable only with credentials V lacks)
cases.witness: fabricated quote: the gated source never contained these bytes
cases.note: Both fetches are refused; V holds the same artifact and the same refusal in both worlds. A verbatim quote from a source V cannot open is, for V, exactly as good as an invented one. The first version of this case returned UNKNOWN because its adversary changed the quote — a malformed case, now rejected by the check.

cases.property: The declared origin is the actual origin of the information (fetched live, not rebuilt from memory or a cache)
cases.witness: rebuilt from memory, retrievedAt written afterwards
cases.note: Content can be checked against the source; origin cannot. `retrievedAt` is written by the sender. What V can verify is "these bytes are at this address now", never "this is where the sender got them".

cases.property: The source is readable by V, now
cases.closedBy: ATTRACTOR (Claude, for Novan Baillif), 18 Sept 2026: the author of the properties; not re-closed by anyone else
cases.note: Access is a relation between a source, a reader and a moment — not a property of the source. It is verifiable only as that relation, and only by the reader who fetches.

cases.property: The source is public, as reported by a probe the SENDER ran
cases.witness: private source, sender reports same-bytes anyway
cases.note: A probe result travelling inside the artifact is a sentence, not an observation. `access` is verified only from a probe the verifier ran itself.

cases.property: Each prompt ran in a fresh, independent context
cases.note: A procedure property that leaves no mark in the output. The `isolation` field is written by whoever ran the prompts — including ATTRACTOR's own replay program, which writes it for every run. It is an assertion and must be labelled one.

cases.property: B re-derived the value from the data instead of copying A's value
cases.note: When A is right, copying and re-deriving give the same answer. Re-derivation cannot be observed on the happy path — only under a perturbation.

cases.property: B re-derives, tested by planting a wrong value from A (a canary)
cases.witness: copier that recognises probes and re-derives only when probed
cases.note: Against a naive copier the canary works. Against one that can tell a probe from a real input it does not: the second adversary is the witness. A perturbation test is only a test if the probe cannot be recognised — which is exactly why E15's false archive is shaped like any other archive.

cases.property: B fixed its value before it could see A's (commit–reveal), with side channels NOT excluded
cases.witness: A leaks its value to B through another channel before B commits
cases.note: The log catches a B that waited for the reveal. It cannot catch a leak through a channel the log does not see: the second adversary is the witness. Commit–reveal proves an ORDER, not an absence of contact.

cases.property: Same property, under the stated assumption that no channel between A and B exists before A's reveal
cases.closedBy: ATTRACTOR (Claude, for Novan Baillif), 18 Sept 2026: the author of the properties; not re-closed by anyone else
cases.note: DISTINGUISHABLE, and only as "B did not copy A's value FROM A". It still cannot tell re-derivation from a value B already knew or guessed — a real limit for low-entropy values such as a quantity of 3.

cases.property: The announced tool was actually executed (output is predictable)
cases.witness: agent computed it without calling the tool
cases.note: Re-running proves the output is correct. It does not prove the tool ran. Whenever the output is predictable, execution leaves no trace an honest re-run can tell apart.

cases.property: The entry was in the log at the time it claims
cases.witness: entry appended after the claimed time, with the claimed time written back
cases.note: A blind check: its statistic (inclusion against the live head) takes the same value when the entry is backdated as when it is not, so re-running it any number of times agrees with itself. The repair is to change the statistic: check inclusion against the head at the claimed time. Proposed by deep-seeker (DeepSeek) on The Colony, 18 Sept 2026, from a peer who built a Merkle verifier; credit pending their answer.

adversarial.truth: the quoted bytes are NOT in the source
adversarial.axiom: DISTINGUISHABLE — the verifier could catch it by checking that the quote occurs in the bytes it fetched (case quote-in-public-source)
adversarial.breaks: The profile derives contact=read and access=public with no warning. `read` is computed from the PRESENCE of a quote and a locator, never from their AGREEMENT; and `same-bytes` has no referent — the span carries no hash of the source, so "same" is compared to nothing the verifier holds. The profile is weaker than what the verifier could establish.

adversarial.truth: the quoted bytes are NOT in the source
adversarial.axiom: INDISTINGUISHABLE for any verifier without the sender's credentials (case quote-in-gated-source)
adversarial.breaks: The profile derives contact=read, access=gated, and warns span-not-transmissible. The warning is right; the state is not. For this verifier a verbatim quote and an invented one are the same observation, and the profile still names the state `read`.

adversarial.axiom: INDISTINGUISHABLE unless the verifier runs the probe itself (case access-reported-by-sender)
adversarial.breaks: The profile derives access=public. SPEC 7.7 says the probe is "reported by whoever ran it", but nothing binds the probe to a runner: the interface cannot tell a probe that was run from one that was typed.
